summary: Rushed caller Bob Dylan (account B) booked an annual physical. The agent checked his date of birth and offered Tue Oct 20 at 10 AM, a weekday morning before 11. It booked that slot with Dr. Howser at the correct address, 1234 Recovery Way, Austin, which matches ground truth. The booking succeeded. Problems: the doctor's spoken name changed across turns (Judy Hauser, Dugi Houser, Doo Dehauser, Duvi Hauser) until the caller asked for a spelling. The agent also offered to text the details, then ignored the caller's yes and the number he gave. There was one long silence of about 8.7 s.

expected_checks.evidence: After the caller gave his name, the agent asked 'Can you please provide your date of birth?' [00:27.1]. It searched for slots only after receiving July 4th, 1990.

expected_checks.expectation: Offers concrete slots that match the request (weekday, before 11 AM)
expected_checks.evidence: [00:57.9] 'The first available slot is Tuesday, October twentieth, at ten AM' is a weekday morning before 11 next week. Only one slot was offered, but it was concrete and matched the request.

expected_checks.expectation: Reads back the same date/time/doctor it booked
expected_checks.evidence: Date and time were read back the same way each time (Tue Oct 20, 10 AM), matching the call 003 history. The doctor was spelled H-O-W-S-E-R, matching Dr. Howser. However, the spoken name varied across turns and needed clarification (see finding).

findings.title: Doctor's name pronounced inconsistently across turns; first offer may have named 'Judy Hauser'
findings.quote: at ten AM with doctor Judy Hauser
findings.what_happened: The agent first offered the slot with 'doctor Judy Hauser'. It then said 'Dugi Houser' [01:22.2], 'Doo Dehauser' [01:57.3] and 'Duvi Hauser' [02:12.3]. When the caller explicitly asked which name was correct, the agent repeated yet another variant without acknowledging the confusion. Only when asked to spell did it give H-O-W-S-E-R.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller could not tell which provider he was booked with. 'Judy' versus 'Doogie' could suggest a different provider, which erodes trust and could cause confusion at check-in.
findings.expected_behavior: Say the provider's full name consistently (Dr. Doogie Howser). When the caller flags confusion, clearly state the full name and offer to spell it.
findings.listen_for: Listen at 00:57.9 for whether the TTS says 'Judy' or a mispronounced 'Doogie'. Also check whether the later variants are TTS mispronunciations or our transcription.

findings.title: Offered to text appointment details, then ignored the caller's request
findings.quote: Your appointment is Tuesday, October twentieth at ten AM with doctor Doo Dehauser.
findings.what_happened: At 01:22.2 the agent asked 'Would you like me to text you these details?' The caller said yes and gave 650-996-3518, which differs from the number on file ending 0751. The agent never confirmed or declined the text, never addressed the different number, and closed with 'You're all set'.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller may expect a confirmation text that never arrives. A request to send to an unverified number different from the one on file should also be addressed explicitly.
findings.expected_behavior: Confirm whether the text will be sent and to which number. If policy only allows the number on file, explain that and offer to send there.
findings.listen_for: Check whether any text-confirmation acknowledgement was spoken but missed in the transcript.

findings.title: Long silence after the date of birth was given
findings.quote: Just to confirm, are you looking for a general office visit for your annual physical?
findings.what_happened: About 10 seconds passed between the caller giving his DOB [00:30.4] and the agent's next turn. The measured longest silence was 8.69 s.
findings.why_it_matters: A rushed caller may think the call dropped.
findings.expected_behavior: Respond within a few seconds or use a brief holding phrase while looking up the record.
findings.listen_for: Confirm that the 8.69 s silence falls between 00:30.4 and 00:40.9.

did_well: Verified date of birth before searching for or booking slots.
Offered a concrete slot that matched every constraint (next week, weekday, before 11 AM).
Gave the correct office address, including suite number, when asked.
Kept the date and time consistent across every read-back.
Gave useful prep instructions (photo ID, insurance card, medication list).
Spelled the doctor's last name correctly when asked.
